My vacation ended after five days. I got back from vacation, and was shocked at my weight. I gained 12 pounds on vacation. On top of that, I started doing much more exercise and lifting weights.
So all-in-all, I gained weight from vacation, and also increased my body fat percentage, which has dropped since then.
My vacation fat gain was due to stress and dehydration, along with not having access to my regular routines. It was stressful, I was busy, and I couldn't work out.
Stress and dehydration cause a decrease in leptin, which is what signals your body that it has enough energy in its fat stores and shouldn't eat at the moment.
And no, I'm not going on vacation ever again.

To understand what causes an abnormal body temperature (also called high temperature or fever), we must first understand how body temperature is determined. There is an important temperature regulator in the brain known as the hypothalamus. As body temperature rises or falls, a message is transmitted to a nerve in this important temperature-regulating brain structure. This message causes the nerve to send back messages that cause changes in other body tissues that help regulate body temperature in response to the signal. This is what keeps body temperature regulated normally.
If body temperature rises above 100 degrees Fahrenheit (37.8 degrees Celsius) in anyone with a child's body, brain stem damage could occur in that child's brain stem with serious consequences.
